message.reasoning:
I'm planning comprehensive JUnit 4 tests for W3CDom covering fromJsoup conversion with null checks, convert method behavior, the W3CBuilder's head/tail handling for different node types, attribute copying with invalid characters, namespace updates, and string serialization.

Since W3CBuilder is a protected static inner class, I'll put my test class in the org.jsoup.helper package to access it. I'm mapping out specific test cases: verifying fromJsoup throws on null input, confirms basic conversion works, checks that convert properly sets or leaves blank the document URI based on the source's base URI, and tests attribute handling for both valid and invalid characters.

I'm also planning coverage for namespace handling (default xmlns, prefixed xmlns, tags without prefixes), the asString output, and node types like text, comments, and script data nodes through full document parsing. I need to confirm the jsoup library itself is available on the classpath since the class under test already depends on it internally.

For the null-input case, I'm checking how Validate.notNull throws an IllegalArgumentException, and planning to assert that behavior directly in a new test class within the org.jsoup.helper package.

I'll test W3CBuilder through its public convert() entry point rather than instantiating it directly, since that's sufficient to exercise its internal logic. I also need to set up a DocumentBuilderFactory so I can build an empty org.w3c.dom.Document for testing convert() with a pre-existing document, covering both branches of how the destination document is determined.

For blank location I expect null since the URI setter is skipped, while non-blank location via Jsoup.parse with a base URI should set the document URI correctly. I'm also planning attribute sanitization tests -- checking that invalid characters in keys get stripped per the XML name pattern, and that keys starting with a digit after sanitization are handled properly since they'd no longer match the valid starting character rule.

Now I need to verify that when sanitization produces an empty string (all characters invalid), the attribute gets dropped since the full-match regex requires at least one valid character. I'm also setting up normal valid attribute cases and namespace resolution tests for elements without a prefix, checking how the namespace stack handles missing xmlns entries.

For elements that declare xmlns inline, I'm checking the order of operations: a new namespace map gets pushed for the current element before updateNamespaces runs, so the xmlns value is available immediately for resolving that same element's own namespace. I want to test this with a div declaring xmlns="urn:test" to confirm self-referential namespace resolution works correctly.

For prefixed namespaces, I'm considering whether jsoup's HTML parser handles colons in tag names reliably, and decide it's safer to use jsoup's XML parser mode to preserve case and structure for these namespace tests.

Now I'm sketching out the individual test cases, starting with one that verifies a null input to the conversion method throws an IllegalArgumentException.

Next I'm checking basic HTML conversion: parsing simple markup with Jsoup, converting it, then asserting the resulting W3C document's root element exists and has the expected tag name. I'm also considering a test for how the location/baseUri is handled when parsing without an explicit base URI, since that value should come through blank.

I want to add further cases: verifying documentURI is set correctly when a baseUri is explicitly provided, checking that text content converts properly, and testing that HTML comments carry over into the converted document.

I'm planning additional cases too: script tags should preserve their raw content as a DataNode, and attribute names need sanitization so invalid characters or names starting with digits get normalized or stripped during conversion.

For attribute sanitization testing, I realize it's better to build Elements programmatically using jsoup's node classes directly rather than parsing HTML strings, since that gives full control over exactly which attribute keys exist without worrying about how the HTML tokenizer handles unusual characters.

Still working out the sanitization...the digit-prefixed attribute gets dropped since it fails the pattern match, but "bad!attr" survives once the "!" is stripped out, leaving "badattr" as a valid key. The triple-exclamation attribute sanitizes down to nothing and gets dropped entirely. Now I need to assemble a root document to hold this test element.

For the document structure, it's easier to parse a minimal HTML skeleton with Jsoup first, then append my custom-built div into the body, which guarantees the proper html/head/body hierarchy needed for the conversion logic to correctly locate the root element.

Now I'm setting attribute values including some invalid ones, appending the div to the body, converting to W3C format, and retrieving the resulting div by tag name to verify its attributes came through correctly.

I'm then testing the "xmlns" attribute case by building a div with a custom xmlns value, converting it through the W3C pipeline, and checking that the resulting element's namespace URI reflects what was set.

For the next test, I want to verify a prefixed tag name like "xyz:foo" with a matching "xmlns:xyz" attribute, so I'm checking whether jsoup's Tag.valueOf permits colons in tag names when building the element programmatically.

I'm uncertain whether Tag.valueOf normalizes case by default, but since W3CDom is the target class, I shouldn't rely on assumptions about Tag's internal behavior—I just need a prefixed tag name with the colon preserved for the test.

Using a lowercase tag like "xyz:foo" sidesteps case concerns since the colon stays intact regardless, and the prefix extraction logic (checking indexOf(":") > 0) will correctly pull "xyz" matching the attribute key. I'm planning the next tests: one verifying no namespace resolves when no xmlns attribute exists anywhere in the ancestry (expecting null), and another about tail text handling.

For the tail-descend test, I want to confirm sibling traversal works correctly by nesting a div with two span children and checking the parser returns to the correct parent after each child's subtree -- if tail handling were broken, the structure would flatten incorrectly instead of preserving proper nesting.

Then for testAsString, I'm parsing a simple paragraph and verifying the serialized output string contains the expected tag markup.

Next I'm considering edge cases like an empty jsoup document, since jsoup always normalizes input into a full html/head/body structure even when the input string is empty, so the conversion should still produce valid output.

I should also verify DataNode handling for script tags and confirm namespace-aware document building only applies when going through fromJsoup, while direct-convert tests using non-namespace-aware builders are fine as long as they don't test namespace URIs specifically.

I'll create a helper method to build an empty document consistently across tests needing a manual Document object for convert(). I'm also confirming that Validate.notNull follows jsoup's standard pattern of throwing an IllegalArgumentException on null input, which is safe to trust as external dependency behavior.

For comment extraction, I'll just check for a substring like "hi" rather than asserting exact whitespace, since Comment node's getData() preserves literal text. I'm finalizing the needed imports for jsoup, DOM, and XML parsing, then adding tests that specifically cover the Comment and DataNode branches separately to maximize branch coverage in the if/else chain.

I also want to hit the final unhandled else branch, triggered by node types like DocumentType that aren't Element/TextNode/Comment/DataNode — testing with a `<!DOCTYPE html>` declaration should trigger this no-op path, though I need to check how convert() traverses only the first child of root.

If convert() only walks `in.child(0)` and the DOCTYPE is sibling to the html element, this could mean the html element gets skipped entirely if DOCTYPE comes first — that looks like a real fault worth demonstrating in a test case, since the task calls for tests that can genuinely catch bugs like this.

If doctype is indeed inserted as child(0) before html when a DOCTYPE is present, then head() would be called on the doctype node, hit the unhandled else-branch, and never append anything to the w3c document — meaning getDocumentElement() would return null entirely. This looks like a genuine bug worth capturing in a test, so I should confirm jsoup's actual child ordering behavior to write a deterministic assertion around it.

Actually relying on jsoup's internal doctype/child ordering behavior would be guessing about external class behavior not present in the given source, which violates the no-guessing rule. I'll avoid that risky assertion and instead construct a controlled Document manually, setting the root's first child directly to test the unhandled branch without depending on parser quirks.

Since I'm unsure of the exact DocumentType constructor signature across jsoup versions, risking a compile error isn't worth it. I'll skip explicitly testing that unhandled-else branch and instead add a comment noting it's not covered due to uncertainty about internal APIs, consistent with the guidance to flag uncertain cases rather than guess.

For test inputs, I'll avoid declaring an explicit DOCTYPE so that child(0) of #root reliably resolves to the html element, which is documented jsoup parser behavior rather than a risky internal assumption. That finalizes the test suite without a problematic doctype case, so now I'm checking StringUtil.isBlank behavior for location handling in Jsoup.parse.

I confirm that Jsoup.parse(String html) defaults to an empty baseUri per the documented API, which is safe to rely on. Now I'll write the final test code, placing the test class in the same package as W3CDom but adding an explicit import for it to satisfy the naming and import requirements.

That duplicate import would just trigger a compiler warning, not an error, so it's fine either way. Now I'm verifying the jsoup API methods I'm using for parsing, DOM access, and attribute handling are correct before finalizing the test with its comments and summary table.

Writing import statements...

I realize there's a naming collision since both jsoup and w3c have classes called Document and Element, so I need to carefully alias or fully qualify them to avoid conflicts.

Setting up test fixtures with a W3CDom instance and a helper method to build a namespace-aware empty w3c Document for direct conversion tests...

I'll also verify fromJsoup behaves correctly on edge cases, like an empty jsoup document still producing a valid html/head/body structure with "html" as the root tag. Once I've covered these scenarios, I'll finalize the test numbering and write the complete Java code followed by a summary table in Thai.
